question: What evidence supports the diagnosis of Acute Inflammatory Polyneuropathy in this patient?

The diagnosis of AIDP in this patient rests on three pillars:  

1. Clinical presentation  
 • Subacute (3-week) progression of symmetrical limb paresthesias and weakness following a mild upper‐respiratory viral prodrome  
 • Absent to diminished deep‐tendon reflexes (areflexia in the legs, UE reflexes L>R)  
 • Sensory “glove-and-stocking” deficits to pinprick (hands up to wrists/elbows; legs from knees down) and positive Romberg sign  
 • Gait disturbance requiring walker assistance  

2. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings (“albuminocytologic dissociation”)  
 • Elevated CSF protein 72 mg/dL (normal 15–45)  
 • Zero CSF white blood cells  

3. Therapeutic response  
 • Clinical improvement in strength and gait with a standard 5-day course of IVIG  

Taken together—ascending, symmetric sensorimotor deficits with hyporeflexia, characteristic CSF profile, and response to immunotherapy—these findings confirm the diagnosis of Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy.
